However, the construction we use does not contradict any upper bound of the form O(n1−α kJk2αF ) for α ∈ [0, 1]. We conjecture that the supremum is, in fact, α = 1/3, so that our bound is optimal in this stronger sense as well. Our methods extend in a straightforward manner not just to Ising models with external fields, but indeed to general higher order Markov random fields, as long as we assume a bound r on the order of the highest interaction (i.e. size of the largest hyper-edge). The results also generalize naturally to the case of non-binary alphabets but for simplicity, we only discuss the binary case.
